name: b-laid-paper-rain
prompt: A portrait newspaper-cartoon drawing in black ink on heavy cream laid paper, the ribbed chain lines and fine crosswise laid lines of the sheet showing through everywhere, so every grey in the picture comes from that ribbed grain catching the ink and from thousands of thin slanting rain strokes, with no wash, no smudged shading and no solid grey fills. Today, a medium-wide view at seated eye level of a plain wooden park bench on wet tarmac: on the left sits a stout, heavily jowled rich man in a tall silk top hat, a dark frock coat buttoned over his round belly, a watch chain across his waistcoat, perfectly dry beneath a large black umbrella he angles over himself alone, his free gloved hand flicking outward at the woman beside him in a bored dismissal, eyes half-closed, chin raised. On the right, out from under the umbrella's edge, a tired hospital nurse in plain scrubs and a thin knitted cardigan sits hunched in the downpour, hair plastered to her forehead, a canvas tote bag held on her lap, looking at him. Behind them, rings spread across puddles that mirror the bench legs, and a modern glass-and-steel bus shelter stands drawn in sparse thin outline. Flat grey overcast daylight, no sun, the umbrella the one deep solid black in the frame. Strictly black ink on cream paper, nothing else. The top third of the picture is an open band of empty ribbed paper with only faint falling rain lines, left clear for a caption. No words, no letters, no signage text, no signature anywhere in the image. Thanks.
